statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-56391: with -w (--check-chars) in a multibyte locale, GNU coreutils uniq's find_field() advances by the length of the first character over and over instead of walking the line, so the compared length is inflated and memcmp reads past the line buffer, which can crash uniq or expose adjacent heap memory (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-56391, https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/25/2). Upstream fixed the loop in https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils/commit/d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371, after the 9.11 release; its NEWS entry says the bug was introduced in coreutils 9.5. The DHI coreutils packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of coreutils 9.8. The first, 9.8-r1, lacks the fix: given two UTF-8 lines that both begin with a two-byte character and an ASCII character and differ only after them (é, a, then 1 or 2), uniq -w2 keeps both lines because it compares four bytes instead of the three those two characters occupy. 9.8-r2 backports the upstream change: on x86_64 and aarch64 the same input collapses to one line, as does the upstream regression test (a four-byte character followed by 255 ASCII characters, with -w256). 9.8-r2 is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-56391: with -w (--check-chars) in a multibyte locale, GNU coreutils uniq's find_field() advances by the length of the first character over and over instead of walking the line, so the compared length is inflated and memcmp reads past the line buffer, which can crash uniq or expose adjacent heap memory (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-56391, https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/07/25/2). Upstream fixed the loop in https://github.com/coreutils/coreutils/commit/d64e35a8a4c0e4608321433e0d84d917e4e36371 (bug introduced in coreutils 9.5); Debian rates it unimportant and lists trixie's 9.7-3 as unfixed. The DHI coreutils packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's coreutils 9.7-3 with that change backported, and the DHI Debian repository publishes two such builds on amd64 and arm64. Tested in all four packages: given two UTF-8 lines that both begin with a two-byte character and an ASCII character and differ only after them (é, a, then 1 or 2), uniq -w2 in the C.UTF-8 locale prints one line, while Debian's own coreutils 9.7-3 on the same systems prints both, because it compares four bytes instead of the three those two characters occupy. The changelog shipped in both builds records the backport. Every published build carries the fix, so the range ends at the lower of the two.
